newsitem.title: CHINA: China to end leaded petrol output by 2000 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China to end leaded petrol output by 2000 - paper.

text.p: China is expected to stop producing leaded petrol by the year 2000 to try to reduce environmental pollution, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

State-run China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) had already started phasing out the use of leaded petrol, which accounted for 40 percent of total consumption last year, the newspaper quoted Zhang Deyi, deputy chief engineer with Sinopec, as saying.
"Growing air pollution in China's big cities makes addressing auto emissions a serious concern," Zhang was quoted as saying by the newspaper, published by the official China Daily.

Authorities had not yet issued regulations on automobile emissions but major cities such as Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou would likely be the first to ban leaded petrol, Zhang said without giving further details.
